podcast.title: First Two-Tone Single; Band Borrowed £700 from Family; B-Side Created The Selector
podcast.body: In March 1979, the Specials borrowed 700 pounds from family and friends to record "Gangsters," the first Two-Tone single, based on a sample from a Prince Buster song. Having only enough money to record the A-side, Jerry Dammers offered the B-side to a friend named Noel Davis, who contributed an instrumental he had recorded with his brother-in-law in his living room in 1977. Dammers remixed the track and included it as the B-side; the song was called "The Selector" — and that became the name of the (then non-existent) band. This shared 7-inch was the beginning of the post-punk ska revival, which was faster and tighter than traditional ska with a greater reliance on horn sections. "Gangsters was the first two-tone single and a fine example of cooperation."
